name: Beaver Dam Flats
description: Flat, sheltered sites behind the beaver's dam. She has been asked to stop rearranging the picnic tables, and has not.

name: Cedar Hollow
description: The ranger station's own campground, at the foot of the Cedar Trail. The showers are hot, and the ranger knows everyone's name by the second night.

name: Deer Meadow
description: An open meadow at the edge of the big trees. The deer come out at dusk and stand very still, as if you're the one being watched.

name: Footprint Ridge
description: Eight walk-in sites on the ridge where the famous footprint was found. The cast is at the ranger station. The footprint is still here, if you know where to look.

name: Huckleberry Bend
description: A bend in the creek with huckleberries in August. The bears know about the huckleberries. Use the food lockers.

name: Loon Point
description: Lakeside sites with a boat ramp. The loons start at sunrise and do not take requests.

name: Mossy Log
description: Twelve sites under the oldest trees in the forest, open all year. Bring a tarp: it's called Mossy Log for a reason.

name: Owl Roost
description: Quiet sites in a stand of cedars. No fires, by order of the owls, who are trying to sleep during the day.

name: Pine Cone Pass
description: High up in the pass, where the pine cones are the size of a ranger's boot. Pitch your tent away from the tallest pines.

name: Raccoon Ridge
description: Shaded sites with a camp store that sells Squatch Snacks. The raccoons have read the hours on the door.

name: Stump Lake
description: The lake with the famous stump on its far shore. Several campers have reported that it moved. It's a stump.

name: Trout Creek
description: Creekside sites, open all year, with the best fishing on the lake. Breakfast is whatever you catch, plus a bowl of Pine Cone Crunch.
